title: Brioche fingerless mitts
subtitle: Squishy brioche rib fingerless mitts with an afterthought thumb.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts worked in two-colour brioche rib, giving a thick, reversible fabric. DK weight, worked in the round. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Two-colour brioche fingerless mitt, synthesised from the traditional brioche stitch and the standard fingerless mitt construction. The brioche stitch is a long-established technique; this sizing and in-the-round construction is new.

knitting.gaugeText: 20 sts × 28 rounds = 10 × 10 cm in two-colour brioche rib unblocked on 4 mm needles. Brioche relaxes substantially after washing.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A knitting stitch that creates a thick, spongy reversible rib by working a yarn over and a slip stitch together on alternate rounds. Two-colour brioche uses two yarns worked in separate passes to produce a fabric with one colour on each side.
Knit the slipped stitch together with its paired yarn over from the previous round. This is the basic brioche decrease used on knit columns.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning to them after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Fingerless mitts in two-colour
brioche rib
, worked in the round in DK wool, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
The construction is seamless, worked in the round using
magic loop

on a long circular. Two-colour brioche works in two alternating passes: Pass A uses yarn A (main), Pass B uses yarn B (contrast). The two passes together complete one round of brioche. The result is a thick, soft fabric with one colour showing on each side. The thumb uses the
afterthought thumb

. Budget about 80 g of each colour (175 m / 190 yards each), both DK weight. Swatch in brioche before casting on: brioche gauge is substantially looser than stocking stitch gauge at the same needle size, and this pattern uses 4 mm needles rather than the standard 3.75 mm DK needle.
What you need

items.name: Yarn A (main colour)
items.qty: 80 g (about 175 m / 190 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Yarn B (contrast colour)
items.qty: 80 g (about 175 m / 190 yards) of the same yarn in a contrasting colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 2: 1 for the beginning of the round, 1 for the thumb position

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge

20 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in two-colour brioche rib, unblocked, on 4 mm needles. Brioche fabric is much stretchier than standard rib; measure the swatch slightly stretched, to about the width it will sit on a hand.
Brioche stitch guide

items.name: Setup round (A)
items.qty: With yarn A: *k1, (yo, slip 1 purlwise)*, repeat to end.

items.name: Pass A
items.qty: With yarn A: *(BRK, yo, slip 1 purlwise)*, repeat to end.

items.name: Pass B
items.qty: With yarn B: *(yo, slip 1 purlwise, BRK)*, repeat to end.

items.name: Repeat
items.qty: Passes A and B form the brioche round. Repeat throughout.

items.name: BRK
items.qty: Brioche knit: knit the slipped stitch together with its yarn over from the previous pass.

content.text: Two-colour brioche requires the yarn not in use to be dropped at the side each pass. The yarns are never twisted around each other; each colour works its own stitches only. The
BRK
looks like a k2tog but works the slipped stitch and its yo as a unit.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using yarn A and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 34 (38, 42) stitches. All sizes are even numbers so brioche pairs join cleanly. Join to work in the round.
Work the setup round in yarn A, then begin Pass A and Pass B alternations. Work brioche for 24 (26, 28) passes total (12, 13, 14 complete rounds). The cuff measures about 8 (9, 10) cm.
Hand and thumb marker

Continue in brioche for 14 (16, 18) more passes. At the midpoint of the hand, mark the thumb: on a Pass A row, work across the first 8 (9, 10) stitches with waste yarn (in the brioche pattern), then slip them back and work them again with yarn A. The waste yarn marks the thumb gap on the palm side.
Hand above thumb
Continue in brioche for a further 14 (16, 18) passes. Work 4 passes of 1x1 rib in yarn A only to create a neat firm edge. Bind off in rib.
Thumb

Remove waste yarn and pick up 8 (9, 10) stitches above and below the gap. Total: 16 (18, 20) thumb stitches. Work 12 (14, 14) passes of two-colour brioche. Work 4 passes of 1x1 rib in yarn A. Bind off in rib.
Common faults

Fabric is ribbed, not puffy: the yarn overs are not being worked together with their slipped stitch on the following pass. Each BRK must take both the slipped stitch and the yarn over off the needle as one unit.
Colours bleed onto the wrong side: one yarn is being twisted around the other when it is set aside. Drop the inactive yarn without crossing it over the active one.
Stitch count increases after several rounds: a yarn over was worked but no BRK consumed it on the following pass. Count stitches every 4 rounds in the first repeat until the rhythm is secure.
Finishing
Weave in all tails in the corresponding colour on the wrong side. Wet-block to open the brioche fabric.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with a wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. The brioche fabric is reversible; both sides are correct sides.
What to try next

A two-colour brioche hat uses the same pass structure at a larger circumference. The same two-colour technique scaled up to a cowl is the most common first brioche project and uses the same needle size.
